subject: Availability attribution for rolling maintenance + gateway partner outage
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@stratohealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: sanjay@edgegateway.io
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Downtime credit request — May 21 rolling maintenance + gateway degradation

Hi Mateo,

We just received the availability tally for May and it looks like Redwood excluded ~98% of the event window for our account because the platform marked it as scheduled rolling maintenance. However, our production traffic saw a sustained 60–80% error rate across two regions (us-east-1 and us-west-2) for ~3.5 hours that day, which clearly affected customer-facing latency and retries.

Additionally, our logs show an upstream partner gateway (EdgeGateway) dropped connections for certain prefixes during that same span — we pasted excerpts in the attached incident-timeline.csv. We understand scheduled maintenance can be excluded per Section 4.2 of the SLA, but this event overlapped with a partner gateway failure and partial degradation on Redwood’s side (route failovers, queue saturations).

We’re asking for:
- A clear explanation of the calculation that led to the exclusion;
- Recalculation with per-route weighting rather than a pure-time-window exclusion; and
- A pro-rated credit based on the observed partial degradation (not a full exclusion).

We’re happy to hop on a quick call today to review traces. Next available: 2pm ET or 4pm ET.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Infrastructure
StratoHealth

[Attachment: incident-timeline.csv]

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex@stratohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Downtime credit request — May 21 rolling maintenance + gateway degradation

Alex —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attached timeline. I’ve looped in Marissa (sales lead) and Monica (Customer Success) so we can coordinate the credit review and technical deep-dive. We’ll start an internal analysis and aim to get you a preliminary response within 48 hours.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Could you confirm which API routes and customer-facing services (endpoint IDs) experienced the 60–80% error rate? The CSV helps but explicit route IDs speed the recalc.
- If you have sample request IDs or traces, please share them (Redwood tracing IDs or full request IDs).

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal cross-check of our maintenance log and partner outage notes (Marissa/Monica will own).
2) Recompute availability using a blended approach (time-weighted + route impact) and provide the math worksheet (we’ll attach the calc-sheet.xlsx).
3) If we confirm partial degradation attributable to Redwood runtime, propose a pro-rated credit and offer a follow-up technical call.

I can do 2pm ET. Monica — can you book a 30-min slot and include Diego/Infra if we need traces?

— Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134

[Attachment: calc-sheet.xlsx — initial template for availability recompute]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@stratohealth.com>, sanjay@edgegateway.io
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Downtime credit request — May 21 rolling maintenance + gateway degradation

Forwarding technical notes from the infra team and my proposed response.

Team — quick summary of our findings so far (internal):
- Redwood scheduled a rolling config push across control-plane hosts that day; the push window overlapped with distinct kernel upgrade windows in us-west-2. On a small percentage of nodes we saw elevated queuing which led to higher error return rates for long-tail requests.
- EdgeGateway reported an external connectivity regression affecting a subset of routing prefixes (Sanjay’s note attached).
- Contract note: Section 4.2 excludes scheduled maintenance when customers are notified within the SLA notice period. However, the SLA also defines "material degradation" separately — and partial, route-specific degradation should not be an automatic full exclusion.

My recommendation for StratoHealth:
- Recompute availability using a blended attribution algorithm: 60% weight on actual successful request impact (route/request-level errors) and 40% on scheduled window time. This approach aligns with our internal fairness rubric for partial-degradation events.
- If the blended calc still shows >0.5% credit, offer a pro-rated credit equal to the computed outage fraction of monthly recurring charges.
- Exclude EdgeGateway-only failures if they’re confirmed to be strictly third-party (we’ll need their incident ticket). If there is any overlap where Redwood route failover increased customer errors, that overlap is Redwood-attributable.

Action items:
- Monica to collect traces and match request IDs to the CSV (Monica: ETA EOD tomorrow).
- Mateo to send a proposed customer-facing email summarizing the calculation and proposed credit.
- Legal: we should attach the signed SLA (contract-SLA-v2.pdf) for reference in the customer communication.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: contract-SLA-v2.pdf]

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex@stratohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, sanjay@edgegateway.io
Date: Tue, 12 May 2027 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed availability recompute and credit — StratoHealth May 21 event

Alex —

Appreciate your patience while we reviewed this. Attached is our recompute workbook (calc-sheet.xlsx) with the blended attribution applied (60% request-impact / 40% scheduled window). Key points:
- We confirmed elevated error rates on routes: /api/v1/infer (endpoint-id: sh-e1), /api/v1/chat (sh-c3). These account for ~72% of the affected traffic in your timeline.
- EdgeGateway issued a partial outage (ticket #EG-2217) that impacted 18% of affected prefixes; where EdgeGateway alone caused the failure we have excluded that traffic from Redwood attribution.
- After blending and removing pure third-party failures, the net credited availability shortfall is calculated at 0.43% of monthly MRC.

Proposed remediation:
1) Issue a one-time pro-rated credit equal to 0.43% of May MRC applied to your next invoice.
2) Offer a post-mortem call with our infra leads and EdgeGateway to align on prevention — proposed window: Thu 5/14 11am ET.
3) Share the recompute worksheet and our calculation transparency doc (link below).

If that works, Monica will generate a formal credit note and I’ll route for signatures. If you’d like a larger concession while we continue the review, let us know and we can escalate to leadership for exception.

Thanks,
— Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
